content_zh:
年关将至，北风呼啸，天地间白茫茫一片。
二狗子穿一件祖传破夹衣，补丁一层压一层，仍然挡不住夹衣里面塞的杂草柳絮往外面钻。
上半身还好点，好歹有件祖传的衣服御寒，下半身的裤子却只有大半截。
裤子长度刚到膝盖，一条裤腿长一条裤腿短，屁股部位磨得变成了纱线，露出半边冻得发紫的屁股蛋。
脚上的破草鞋也掉了一只，在雪地上留下两行深浅不一的脚印。
此刻二狗子将一小堆柴火捆好，大概有三十多斤，扛回去应该可以交差了。
现在捡柴并不容易，家家户户都要烧柴火，树木根本长不过来。
他走了七八里路，忙了大半天，才从雪地里扒出这些柴。
捆好柴之后，一屁股坐在柴火上，对着双手呵了几口热气，才塞进腋下捂住。
喘了几口气，从破夹衣里掏出一团糠饼，狠狠咬下一大口，用力咀嚼。
糠饼里面掺了大量的谷糠和野菜，还有少量的橡子和草籽，咽下去的时候刮得喉咙生痛。
这玩意说是饼，其实是他从猪食里偷出来的。
纵使是这样的糠饼，他也很少吃饱过。
一个糠饼吃完，舔了舔手指上的残渣，从地上随手抓了一把雪塞进嘴里吞下。
又坐了一会，感觉身体恢复了一些力量，这才起身背起柴火准备回家。
只是他刚才起猛了，又背着几十斤柴，脚下一滑溜，连人带柴就向山坡下摔去。
“碰！碰……啪！”
二狗子趴在地上，痛得腰直不起来。
刚才摔倒的时候，有一个很硬的东西撞在他腰子上。
把他衣服都蹭破一个大洞，腰上还蹭出一道血口子。

伸手在雪地上一阵乱摸，很快就从积雪下面摸出一件大家伙。
这是一只看起来很普通的黄皮葫芦，大约有一尺高，直径最大的地方起码有人头那么大。
葫芦顶部的盖子上面，还沾着他腰上的少许血迹。
此刻那一点点血迹正在消失，似乎都渗进了葫芦之中。
打开葫芦盖子，发现里面混沌的一片，什么都看不清。
二狗子心中琢磨着，这玩意用来装水很不错。
他每天在外面干活，很多时候都喝不到水。
只是这只葫芦还太大了一点，如果能小点就好了。
心中才刚刚升起这个念头，葫芦竟然真的缩小了一大圈。
二狗子有点不敢相信自己的眼睛，揉了揉眼睛，确认葫芦真的只有七八寸高了。
“再小点！”
这一次，二狗子可是瞪大了双眼盯着手里的葫芦。
content_en:
The New Year is approaching, the north wind is howling, and the sky and earth are completely white.
Ergouzi was wearing a torn jacket inherited from his ancestors, with patches layered on top of each other, but it still couldn't stop the weeds and catkins stuffed inside the jacket from getting out.
The upper body was better, as I had an ancestral piece of clothing to keep out the cold, but the lower body only had more than half of the trousers on it.
The length of the trousers just reached the knees, with one trouser leg longer and the other shorter. The buttocks were worn to the point of turning into yarn, exposing half of the buttocks which were purple from the cold.
One of the broken straw shoes on his feet also fell off, leaving two lines of footprints of different depths on the snow.
At this moment, Ergouzi tied up a small pile of firewood, which weighed about thirty kilograms. He should be able to carry it back and deliver it.
It is not easy to collect firewood now. Every household has to burn firewood and trees cannot grow at all.
He walked seven or eight miles and worked for most of the day before he pulled out the firewood from the snow.
After bundling the firewood, he sat down on the firewood, breathed hot air into his hands for a few times, and then stuffed them under his armpits to cover them.
After taking a few breaths, he took out a ball of bran cake from his torn jacket, took a big bite, and chewed hard.
The bran cake is mixed with a large amount of grain bran and wild vegetables, as well as a small amount of acorns and grass seeds, which makes the throat sore when swallowed.
This thing is said to be a cake, but he actually stole it from the pig food.
Even with such bran cake, he was rarely full.
After finishing a bran cake, he licked the residue on his fingers, grabbed a handful of snow from the ground, stuffed it into his mouth and swallowed it.
After sitting for a while, I felt that my body had regained some strength, and then I got up and carried the firewood to prepare to go home.
It's just that he got up violently just now and was carrying dozens of kilograms of firewood on his back. His feet slipped and he fell down the hillside with the firewood.
"Touch! Touch...pop!"
Ergouzi lay on the ground, unable to straighten his back in pain.
When he fell just now, something very hard hit him on the waist.
There was a big hole in his clothes and a bloody gash on his waist.
He reached out and groped around in the snow, and soon pulled out something big from under the snow.
This is an ordinary-looking yellow-skinned gourd, about a foot tall, and its largest diameter is at least as big as a human head.
The lid on the top of the gourd was still stained with a little blood from his waist.
At this moment, the little bit of blood was disappearing, and it seemed that it had seeped into the gourd.
When I opened the lid of the gourd, I found that it was so chaotic inside that I couldn't see anything clearly.
Ergouzi thought to himself, this thing is very good for holding water.
He works outside every day and often has no access to water.
It's just that this gourd is a little too big. It would be better if it could be smaller.
Just when this thought came up in my mind, the gourd actually shrank by a large circle.
Ergouzi couldn't believe his eyes. He rubbed his eyes and confirmed that the gourd was really only seven or eight inches tall.
"Smaller!"
This time, Ergouzi stared at the gourd in his hand with wide eyes.
